newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen opening flat to lower, eyes data.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen opening flat to lower, eyes data.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open flat to lower, with direction coming from inflation data and reaction to Monday's Intel Corp earnings.

Analysts said markets would be taking their cue in part from the Labor Department's March Consumer Price Index (CPI), due out at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. A consensus estimate by economists calls for a 0.2 percent rise overall and a 0.3 percent upswing excluding volatile food and energy prices.
A strong CPI could spur the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates next month.

"It's going to be a mixed to lower market unless the (economic) numbers are weaker than expected ... and I would base that on the poor performance of Intel after the market closed yesterday," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.

Intel, the world's biggest semiconductor maker, reported strong first quarter earnings after the market closed Monday. However, it also warned its second quarter would be flat to only a little better than its first.
Intel dropped almost three points in after-hours trading in New York. In London, Intel dropped three to 130-1/4.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street said Intel failed to deliver the rosy outlook for upcoming quarters that could have signaled a rebound in the high-tech sector.
"A lot depends on the CPI and Intel will direct the high-tech sector," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities, said, "The Intel disappointment is setting in and that is coloring the opening."
In Tokyo, the Nikkei Average rose 241.12 points, or 1.36 percent, to close at 17,933.59.
In London, the FTSE 100 index was up 13.3 at 4265. Despite Intel's drop, most U.S. stocks were firmer in London.
The dollar eased to 126.21/31 against the yen in Tokyo. The greenback in Europe steadied at 1.7324/34 against the mark and at 126.20/25 against the yen.
The U.S. Treasury 30-year bond was up 7/32 to yield 7.15 percent. The Standard & Poors 500 futures index was up 0.10 at 747.40.
